title: Replying to @chrishone My Hot Broadway Tea Take: Reviews Don’t Really...
transcript: so this person asked a very interesting question they asked “if the reviews for Great Gatsby on Broadway are terrible” [which it did not get good reviews] “why are people giving their money to see a terrible production?” and I think sometimes we forget the long history of mega hits on Broadway that did not get good reviews Lea Miserables when it premiered in London at the Royal Shakespeare Company did not get good reviews at all and became one of the biggest hits in musical theatre history The Phantom of the Opera did not get wonderful glowing reviews and became the longest running musical on Broadway and famously Wicked on Broadway got close to terrible reviews there's this famous clip of all the critics and Broadway press people right before the Tony Award is the year that Wicked lost Best Musical talking about how much they hate Wicked “I think Wicked is totally mediocre” “there's nothing to be said about Wicked””Wicked “i found  kind of preachy to tell the truth” “but then you have Wicked this season which opened again to mixed to critical to negative reviews and that appears to be making a run for it” “maybe the one that overcomes the reviews you didn't care for” “no I didn't” “a lumbering bore I think you called it?” “probably I think that's familiar” “👼I liked it👼” “lumbering and boringand overproduced and hard to follow” “it has a lot of problems - its muddled” “it’s messy” “and it's making a million dollars a week so that's shows you our influence” and it turns out those bad reviews didn't matter on the flip side most of the original run of Stephen Sondheim musicals Follies a Little Night Music Pacific Overture Sweeney Todd got great reviews but did not make money during their initial Broadway run Sweeney Todd made money on tour but close to none of those sun high musicals that revolutionized Broadway and got glowing reviews close to none of them made money on Broadway theater critics like to pretend like they have this giant pedestal and they decide what runs and what doesn't and maybe that was the case twenty five years ago Onward in that direction of time and even people on the theatertok like to pretend like I can close a show with a snap of my fingers and if that was true The Great Gatsby would have never opened on Broadway and the reality is the public and the public alone pick what shows they want to run not the critics definitely not theater influencers but the public and the public alone and we have to be honest here I hated The Great Gatsby on Broadway with absolutely everything in my heart and soul but it's selling a ton of tickets right now it's basically selling out the Broadway Theatre which I understand they have the back of the balcony closed off but I did not think they would ever do this well we have to admit that the critics at this point have not really mattered to The Great Gatsby on Broadway because unfortunately they've been very successful because audiences pick what runs not critics and I say that as a certified hater of Wicked, most of Phantom Of the Opera, and The Great Gatsby on Broadway I love the staging of the Hal Prince Phantom of the opera and I actually like Les Mis even though it's two hours of French complaining -every song's a complaint
